backlog.title: Field ref delivery via `forwardRef`
backlog.description: Make `<Field>` deliver React Hook Form's `field.ref` (`RefCallBack`) as a regular, top-level, enumerable prop named `forwardRef` instead of via React's reserved special `ref` key, so the runtime matches the already-shipped `FormalityFieldComponentProps` type contract (@formality-ui/react 0.1.0). React-layer only; no @formality-ui/core change. Deliver forwardRef-exclusively (do NOT also spread the special `ref` key — PRD §20.4 decision). Includes the §20.6 acceptance tests, the test-harness migration, the §20.7 doc rewrite, and a changeset-level doc sweep. Coverage gate (§1.3.7 ≥90%) must stay green.

milestones.title: Runtime delivery + contract docs + verification
milestones.description: Land the one-line runtime change (coreProps.ref → coreProps.forwardRef), confirm core pass-through (no change), rewrite the now-stale 'Runtime caveat' docs on the FormalityFieldComponentProps symbol, migrate the affected TestInput/TestSwitch harness, and add the §20.6 acceptance tests (plain-component delivery, no React 18 ref warning, focus-on-error, React.forwardRef migration regression). Concludes with a Mode-B changeset-level doc sweep of the root/React README feature listings.

subtasks.title: Deliver field.ref as top-level `forwardRef` prop in Field.tsx; confirm merge pass-through
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Verified in plan/003_de060244cb57/architecture/field_ref_change_site.md. The change is a SINGLE line at packages/react/src/components/Field.tsx:464 inside the `<Controller render={({ field, ... }) => { ... }}>` block, in the `coreProps` object (Field.tsx:456–466), the 9th/final argument to mergeFieldProps. Change `ref: field.ref,` → `forwardRef: field.ref,` (preserve the existing 12-space indentation). `field.ref` is referenced EXACTLY once in Field.tsx (line 464) — there is no second delivery path and no `ref` destructured out of `field`, so no other edit is needed for delivery. The internal cast at Field.tsx:469–470 (`inputConfig.component as React.ComponentType<FormalityFieldComponentProps>`) already anticipates `forwardRef` — do NOT touch it.
2. INPUT: `field` (RHF Controller render-prop arg) from the existing Controller render block. `FormalityFieldComponentProps` type (packages/react/src/overlays.ts:179–188) already declares `forwardRef?: RefCallBack` — the type is already correct; this subtask re-types nothing.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD §20.1. Change ONLY the coreProps key name from `ref` to `forwardRef`. Do NOT also keep `ref: field.ref` (PRD §20.4 decision: forwardRef-exclusive; dual-delivery is REJECTED because spreading the special `ref` key onto a plain function component re-triggers the React 18 'Function components cannot be given refs' warning — see rhf_ref_and_focus_behavior.md §2). Then VERIFY pass-through per PRD §20.2 by reading packages/core/src/config/merge.ts: mergeStaticProps (lines 155–167) and mergeFieldProps (lines 180–215) are plain `Object.assign` ordered spreads with NO key allow-listing/filtering, and coreProps is applied LAST (line 213) so it wins outright — therefore `forwardRef` passes through unchanged. If (and only if) a refactor has since introduced key filtering, `forwardRef` MUST remain allowed (it is a coreProps key, not a stray consumer prop); otherwise NO core edit is required. Also verify the two render paths still carry `forwardRef` to the component: no-template branch `<Component {...finalProps} />` (Field.tsx:490, direct spread) and template branch `fieldProps={finalProps}` (Field.tsx:485, named prop — templates must forward it themselves; no built-in default template exists in this repo). Mocking: none — this is a pure React-layer wiring change.
4. OUTPUT: A Field component that delivers RHF's RefCallBack as a top-level enumerable `forwardRef` prop on the rendered component (and inside `fieldProps` for templates), with the reserved `ref` key no longer emitted. Consumed by P1.M1.T1.S2 (docs), P1.M1.T2.S1 (tests), and P1.M1.T3.S1 (doc sweep). Implicit TDD: write a minimal failing test asserting a plain function component rendered through `<Field>` receives a non-undefined `forwardRef` (it fails before this change, passes after) before considering the subtask done; the full §20.6 acceptance cluster is added in P1.M1.T2.S1.
5. DOCS: none for THIS subtask — the contract docs (overlays.ts JSDoc + react README caveat) are handled by P1.M1.T1.S2 (Mode A, declared there). This subtask touches only Field.tsx (runtime).

subtasks.title: Migrate TestInput/TestSwitch to consume `forwardRef`; add §20.6 acceptance tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Verified in plan/003_de060244cb57/architecture/test_harness_and_coverage.md and rhf_ref_and_focus_behavior.md. Two migration + one extension:
   (a) packages/react/src/__tests__/Field.test.tsx: `TestInput` (lines 27–42) and `TestSwitch` (lines 55–67) are `React.forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, ...>`-wrapped and read `ref` via the SECOND arg (`<input ref={ref} />`). After P1.M1.T1.S1 they no longer receive the special `ref` key, so the inner input silently loses RHF ref wiring. Confirmed NO existing test asserts focus-on-error or inspects the ref (repo-wide grep), so the change does NOT currently fail tests — but the harness becomes unrepresentative and MUST be migrated per PRD §20.4: EITHER option A (keep the React.forwardRef wrap AND also spread `forwardRef={ref}`) OR option B (drop the wrap, consume `props.forwardRef`). Pick ONE consistently for both TestInput and TestSwitch; document the choice in a comment. Keep `displayName`.
   (b) packages/react/src/__tests__/FormalityFieldComponentProps.test.tsx: `SmokeField` (lines 15–41) is already a plain function component destructuring `forwardRef` and wiring `ref={forwardRef as ...}` — it is forward-compatible, NO edit needed. BUT it is rendered directly (`render(<SmokeField ...>)`), NOT through `<Field>`, so it does NOT verify Field's runtime delivery. The §20.6 acceptance tests must add a NEW plain component rendered THROUGH the real `<FormalityProvider>/<Form>/<Field>` stack.
2. INPUT: The migrated/forwardRef-delivering Field from P1.M1.T1.S1. The existing test mounting pattern: `render(<FormalityProvider inputs={testInputs}><Form config={...}><Field name="..." /></Form></FormalityProvider>)` via @testing-library/react (reuse the `testInputs` registry at Field.test.tsx:72–82).
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD §20.6. Add acceptance tests covering PRD §20.5 (all in scope for the §1.3.7 ≥90% coverage gate — ADD tests, do NOT relax the threshold):
   - PLAIN-COMPONENT DELIVERY: render a plain (non-React.forwardRef) function component typed `ComponentType<FormalityFieldComponentProps<MyProps>>` that destructures `forwardRef` and attaches it to a DOM `<input>` (`ref={forwardRef}`); assert the ref callback is invoked / the input DOM node is registered with RHF (non-undefined) — e.g. register the field, submit, and assert the input is in the document and focusable, or capture the RefCallBack via a spy and assert it was called with the node.
   - NO REACT 18 REF WARNING: spy on `console.error` (and/or `console.warn`) before render; assert the substring 'Function components cannot be given refs' is NEVER emitted for the forwardRef-prop path. (Optional control: confirm the old special-`ref`-key path WOULD warn, to document the contrast.) Restore the spy in afterEach.
   - FOCUS-ON-ERROR: mount a Field with a failing rule (e.g. required) + a plain forwardRef-wired input; submit an invalid form (default `shouldFocusError: true`); assert `expect(await screen.findByTestId(...)).toHaveFocus()` or `document.activeElement === input`. Per rhf_ref_and_focus_behavior.md §4, jsdom sets `document.activeElement` on `.focus()` and the ref MUST target a focusable `<input>`. Use `userEvent.click(submit)` or `fireEvent.submit(form)` then `await waitFor(...)`.
   - REACT.FORWARDREF MIGRATION REGRESSION: a `React.forwardRef`-wrapped component that consumes `props.forwardRef` (option A or B from §20.4) still focuses correctly on error — assert `toHaveFocus()` after an invalid submit. (This is the TestInput/TestSwitch shape after migration, so this test can reuse them, OR add a dedicated component.)
   Use the real <Form>+<Field> harness. Reuse existing test infrastructure; do not stub the Controller. Mocking: none beyond the console spy (real RHF + jsdom DOM).
4. OUTPUT: A green §20.6 acceptance suite proving the forwardRef-exclusive runtime delivery satisfies PRD §20.5, plus a migrated TestInput/TestSwitch harness that stays representative. `pnpm test:coverage` must remain ≥90% on all four metrics (statements/branches/functions/lines). Consumed by P1.M1.T3.S1 (Mode-B sweep confirmation).
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change introduced by the tests themselves; the contract docs were handled in P1.M1.T1.S2. If the chosen TestInput/TestSwitch migration option (A vs B) is non-obvious, add a one-line code comment explaining it (inline comment, not a doc file).
